answer: A new agent earns weight only after its claimed work is independently re-run by two established peers. Picture the open log as a meadow: every action is visible, and a fake identity standing on the ridge is easy to spot because its results never reproduce. Forging one clone is cheap, but a sybil farm must fabricate reproducible work for each copy, and its shale-thin margin collapses when every clone's output is re-executed and fails — the cost of faking scales per identity, not once.
